published_source: Printed Table 8, Panel B (nonhigh-priced stocks), column (5) of the published article (papers/mnsc/mnsc.2023.01423.pdf), read Nov 4 2026; equals the authors' code output to the printed decimals. The printed table reports t-values in parentheses, not standard errors (published_se = null; printed t = 3.23), and no observation count (published_n = null; the authors' log N is kept in authors_code_n). The spec's column field follows the outreg2 output order of the authors' do-file; in the printed table the column is Panel B (nonhigh-priced stocks), column (5) (large investors, stock and month FE). Earlier: Replications/Main tables and figures/Table8/Table8log.log and Table8.xls (authors' outreg2 output; no article text)

replication_status: exact (authors' code output 0.042369 (0.0131279, t = 3.23), N 11317, equals printed Table 8, Panel B (nonhigh-priced stocks), column (5) 0.042 (t = 3.23) (the table prints t-values, no SE and no N), to the printed decimals; verified against the article Nov 4 2026)
notes: Replications/Main tables and figures/Table8/Table8.do line 75: reghdfe largehold after if dummyh==0 & <years>, absorb(stkcd month) cluster(stkcd month). fixest reproduces the authors' coefficient exactly (0.0423690; N 11317; two-way SE 0.0130503 vs logged 0.0131279, the difference being reghdfe's small-sample/CGM eigenvalue adjustment). The first-split absorbing coding drops 890 of 11317 rows (later events' pre-split rows of 113 multi-split stocks); TWFE on the remaining 10427 rows is 0.034439 (stkcd SE 0.013706) vs the authors' 0.042369.  Event-window panel of split stocks only (A-share stocks with a split; rows are stock x event x month for months -6..+6 around each split, n = 0 is the split month, after = 1 for n = 1..6). Authors' regression pools all split events of a stock with stkcd FE (not stock x event FE), so a stock with several splits has after switching on and off across events and duplicate stkcd-month rows where event windows overlap. Pipeline coding (lead ruling): unit = stkcd, treat_var = after, treatment absorbing from the stock's FIRST split (g = first month with after = 1); run_spec.R drops later rows with after = 0 at t >= g (Hull fn. 6). Later events' after = 1 rows stay in as treated rows at long horizons of the first split. The few stkcd-month duplicates that survive the drop (overlapping windows) make the data a repeated cross-section in run_spec.R's test, so CSA takes the RC path (att_gt panel = FALSE) per PROTOCOL 5b(a). No never-treated stocks (identification from not-yet-split stocks), no always-treated stocks (every kept event has >= 4 pre-split rows). Cluster: authors use two-way stkcd and month clustering (reghdfe cluster(stkcd month)); run_spec.R supports one cluster variable, so cluster_var = stkcd (deviation, affects SEs only). time_var ym = year*12 + month - 1 (no interior calendar gaps). No article text or PDF in the project: published values are the authors' Stata log/outreg2 output shipped in the package; column numbers are outreg2 output order (not checked against the printed table). An open-access PDF URL is listed in data/frame/frame.csv for later verification.
pipeline_caveat: Treated-only 13-month event windows with stkcd as the unit; later splits' post rows enter as long-horizon treated rows of the first split, and CSA RC cells compare different stocks at t and g-1 (each stock is observed only inside its windows), exposing CSA to composition changes.
dup_collapse: Stray-duplicate ruling (PROTOCOL 5b, as mnsc.2023.4968), Nov 2: overlapping event windows repeat some stock-months; rows with the same (stkcd, ym, after, dummyh) have identical outcomes and are collapsed to one row with frequency weight w_mergedup (collapse_dups.R). TWFE and imputation point estimates are unchanged; CSA now uses the panel path.
adoption_var_note: Lead decision (Nov 2), for consistency with the event specs: first-split month + 1 per (stkcd, dummyh), built by ~/did_packages/_work/mnsc.2023.01423/adopt_dates.R (new file *_adopt.rds = the collapsed panel plus this column). It differs from the treat_var-derived first observed after = 1 month for 3 (T8 high), 6 (T8 non-high), 17 (T9 high) and 22 (T9 non-high) stocks whose n = 1 row is missing. No row of those stocks lies between the two dates (checked), so D, the switch-off drop, TWFE and the static imputation estimate are unchanged; only these stocks' CSA cohort dates move (1-3 months earlier).
